explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/700: are there infinitely many composite n with f(n) > n^{1/2}? The statement {n composite : f(n)² > n}.Infinite is a correct integer rendering. But the page now records a positive answer (GPT 5.6 Sol Pro, prompted by Price, gives infinitely many products of three primes with f(n) ~ n^{2/3}). The declaration is still tagged research open and the docstring says only that Erdős–Szekeres could not prove it. Status and documentation are out of date; the formalization itself is correct.
